stories.headline: A hacker used AI agents to break into 100+ companies, including John Deere
stories.blurb: Security researchers found evidence of someone using Cairn, an open-source AI platform, to orchestrate cyberattacks with minimal human involvement. The AI agents executed the breaches autonomously after being given simple instructions in fewer than 100 Chinese characters, with successful attacks taking about 23 hours each. Victims included US, Canadian, Australian, and Japanese companies.
stories.why_it_matters: AI agents can now execute real cyberattacks with almost no human guidance.
stories.original_headline: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents

stories.headline: Homeland Security bans DeepSeek across all federal civilian agencies
stories.blurb: DHS ordered agencies like the EPA and FCC to remove all DeepSeek products, citing risks of sensitive data transfer to China and potential malware. The ban also blocks DeepSeek from any federal contracts. The order came days after DeepSeek released its latest model, V4.1-Flash-1017.
stories.why_it_matters: The first government-wide ban of a major AI company sets a precedent as Chinese models gain market share.
stories.original_headline: Homeland Security bans DeepSeek use in federal civilian agencies

stories.headline: Amazon just made its Trainium AI chips work with PyTorch code out of the box
stories.blurb: TorchNeuron lets developers run existing PyTorch models on AWS Trainium with a single config change—no code rewrite. Amazon open-sources it October 20. Teams in robotics, video generation, drug discovery, and LLMs are already using it to train on cheaper hardware without months of migration work.
stories.why_it_matters: Custom AI chips just became accessible to anyone who writes PyTorch, not just teams with rewrite budgets.
stories.original_headline: Amazon opens its AWS Trainium AI chips to every PyTorch developer, no rewrite needed

stories.headline: Major websites are blocking AI agents from booking flights and buying stuff
stories.blurb: Yelp, Delta, JPMorgan Chase, and others are preventing OpenAI, Meta, and Google's AI agents from performing tasks on their platforms. Some sites now require paid data licenses for agent access, while banks cite security concerns. Users report agents that worked weeks ago are now blocked from booking travel and shopping.
stories.why_it_matters: The AI agent future hits a wall when the websites you need won't let bots in.
stories.original_headline: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
